summary: Ochoco NF summit in Crook County, OR: a 1930s cabin, a 1950s timber tower gone by 1972, and communication equipment on the summit today.

facts.design: Cabin in the 1930s, then a timber tower in the 1950s: treated timber R-6 per FFLOS, enclosed L-4 per firelookout.com
facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1972 (removed, destroyed or burned, depending on the source); the summit now has a communication tower

staffing.status: Carol Lochrie listed as known lookout personnel; no later staffing in the sources read

access.note: A trail listing gives trailheads at Walton Lake and near Lookout Mountain; no source describes limits at the communication site

visit.trail_note: Trailheads at Walton Lake (north) and near Lookout Mountain (south), per a trail listing

facts.elevation_ft: 6,755 per Komoot; 6,753 per firelookout.com and FFLOS
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Ochoco National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Komoot gives 6,755 ft; firelookout.com and FFLOS give 6,753 ft. The story gives 6,755 ft and notes the firelookout.com figure.
FFLOS says removed in 1972; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1972; the trail listing says burned down in a fire in 1972. The story reports all three.
FFLOS calls the 1950s tower a treated timber R-6 tower; firelookout.com calls it an enclosed L-4 tower. Both are reported; the design is not settled.

notes_for_editor: Brief kind 'two_story' is not supported by these sources, which describe a 1930s cabin and then a 1950s tower; left unchanged for review. Neither the brief nor the sources give a usable height (FFLOS '10'' may refer to a cab), so no height is set. The Forest Service AT&T Round Mountain record calls the site Round Mt., about 5 miles south of Walton Lake, and does not mention a summit; the link to the summit's communication tower is inferred from the name, the location and the trail listing. Komoot is a trail listing and is weak evidence for the 1972 fire and the trailheads. The -2 Round Mountain record (us-or-round-mountain-2) is a different site on the Deschutes NF.
